chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I have not seen the people take from al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) anything except the prayer after 'Asr and after al-Ghada (morning prayer) during the circumambulation of the obligatory [pilgrimage].
And whoever forgets these two rak'ahs until he dies, his guardian should perform them on his behalf.

key_terms.الْغَدَاة: The morning prayer (specifically referring to the prayer after Fajr in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets the recommended prayers during Tawaf and dies before making them up?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the established Sunnah of performing two rak'ahs during the obligatory Hajj tawaf, linking this practice directly to the traditions of Imam al-Hasan and Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon them). It further establishes the legal principle of *qada* (make-up prayer) by a guardian (*wali*) if the pilgrim passes away before fulfilling this specific voluntary act, underscoring the continuity of ritual observance beyond death.
